premisesReverified: External mechanism confirmed live: an unkeyed request to a.basemaps.cartocdn.com/dark_all/... returns HTTP 200 (not an error status) with a 5183-byte 'API KEY REQUIRED' watermark PNG -- a naive status-code check would have missed this defect entirely.

CONTRADICTED: the dispatch's premise 'the keyed raster service uses new style paths (rastertiles/<style>)' is wrong for our two named styles. CARTO's own docs.carto.com/faqs/carto-basemaps migration table maps dark_all to a VECTOR style (dark-matter-gl-style/style.json), not a renamed raster path. The rastertiles/ prefix belongs only to the newer voyager style family. Ground truth from CartoDB/basemap-styles (the style-list source of truth): dark_all and light_only_labels are still valid keyed style paths at their EXISTING bare location -- the fix is appending ?key=, nothing else.

Live-verified both ways with the real Secret Manager key: (a) bare 'dark_all' + key -> HTTP 200, 126 bytes, a real dark tile (visually confirmed, no watermark); (b) 'rastertiles/dark_all' + key -> also 200/126 bytes identical (CARTO's CDN does not strict-validate the prefix either way, but the bare path is the documented, current name so that is what ships). light_only_labels + key -> HTTP 200, 139 bytes, blank/transparent (correct for a labels-only tile over open water, not a watermark).

CARTO_API_KEY in Secret Manager is 38 bytes on disk with a trailing CR-CR-LF (
), i.e. 35 real characters -- matches the dispatch's stated '35 chars' exactly once trimmed. A naive `tr -d '
'` alone (stripping LF only) leaves a stray  in the key and silently breaks it; both  and 
 must be stripped.
designDecisions: New shared module packages/map-renderer/src/map/carto-key.js (cartoApiKey, keyedCartoTileUrls) consumed by both gis-map-paint.js and basemap-labels.js, rather than duplicating the key-read/URL-build logic in each file.

basemap-labels.js's CARTO_LABELS_TILES (a frozen constant array) became cartoLabelsTiles() (a function) since the URL now depends on a runtime-read env value rather than being a static literal. Updated its one internal consumer (labelsSourceSpec) and its one external test consumer (map-legend.test.js) accordingly.
import.meta.env?.VITE_CARTO_API_KEY guarded by `typeof import.meta !== "undefined"`, matching this repo's own existing iccCitation.ts convention -- not a new pattern.

Verified via built dist output (tsup, this package's bundler, NOT Vite) that `import.meta.env?.VITE_CARTO_API_KEY` survives into the ESM build (dist/index.js) as literal, unreplaced source -- tsup/esbuild warns 'import.meta is not available with cjs' for the CJS build (where it correctly resolves to undefined via optional chaining, never throwing) but leaves it untouched in ESM, which is what property-explorer's Vite build consumes and where Vite's own import.meta.env replacement then applies. This exact pattern already has a live precedent in the SAME compiled output: `import.meta.env?.VITE_PARCEL_PMTILES_HASH || "b692c6534d26"` -- an existing, already-shipped instance of a Vite env var read inside this same tsup-built package, which is what gives this design real confidence beyond theoretical reasoning about bundler interop.

Vercel VITE_CARTO_API_KEY added to property-explorer production env (was not previously set) from the trimmed Secret Manager value. Vercel's own CLI warned 'will be visible to anyone visiting your site' on add -- expected and correct per the dispatch's own framing (publishable client-side key, domain-restricted at the CARTO dashboard, not a secret).
